evidence.foliage: Deciduous broadleaf; crown spreads with age. A single year-round opacity is not a botanical constant.
evidence.sizeContext: 20–25 m height and 18–20 m spread are South Australian landscape guidance, not universal maxima. Virginia Tech lists 100 ft height and 80 ft spread (approximately 30.5 m and 24.4 m). Site, cultivar, age and pruning affect dimensions.
evidence.spacingContext: Published crown spread does not establish a minimum trunk-to-trunk distance or a unique sustainable stand density. The current 20 m placement exclusion is a prototype modelling assumption, not CS2 asset geometry or a measured species requirement.

quantitativeShadeEvidence.note: The cited sources provide qualitative light preferences, not calibrated light-transmission or survival percentages. Runtime values 60 and 50 remain placeholders pending a defined light model and supporting measurements.

evidence.rhsHardiness: H6; winter minimum category -20 to -15 C, not an annual-temperature suitability curve
evidence.light: Full sun preferred; partial shade tolerated
evidence.soil: Broad soil tolerance; moist, well-drained soil preferred
evidence.estimates: 20 m spacing is a planting choice informed by crown spread. Temperature and slope curves, elevation limits, canopy opacity and shade percentage are provisional authoring estimates, not measured survival thresholds. Native CS2 controls aging and survival; this profile only influences initial placement. Canopy/shade values are descriptive until shading simulation is implemented. Age percentages are user-selected initial proportions, not botanical observations.
